extracted.intended_audience: EPA rulewriters and regulators, primacy states, water systems, policymakers, and stakeholders participating in the LCRI notice-and-comment process
extracted.subtask_description: Public comments on the EPA's proposed Lead and Copper Rule Improvements (LCRI), offering specific regulatory requirements, definitions, compliance timelines, monitoring and sampling protocols, enforcement and reporting expectations, materials guidance, and environmental justice safeguards the final rule should adopt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require full replacement of 100% of lead service lines (LSLs) irrespective of ownership and paid by water systems
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should require that water systems replace all lead service lines (LSLs) and that water systems, localities, and states overcome any barriers or EPA will retain primacy for the LCRI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule must require full LSL replacements at no direct cost to customers; presume water systems have control over full service lines; primacy states should adopt rules ensuring systems have authority to fully replace lines; prohibit charging customers for full replacements; implement accountability for claims of barriers to access.

rubrics_metrics.name: LSL replacement within 10 years (no long extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: LSL replacement in 10 years or less is necessary and feasible; the LCRI cannot authorize extensions beyond 10 years for systems that would be required to remove large numbers of LSLs per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate or substantially narrow/shorten extensions; allow extensions only in truly exceptional circumstances with public notice, comment, and local hearing; include mandatory minimum annual replacement numbers; do not permit systems with many LSLs to avoid removing them within 10 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory minimum annual LSLR rates
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should include a mandatory minimum number of annual LSLRs to ensure timely replacement across systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set enforceable minimum replacement rates (numeric) tailored to system size/concentration of LSLs; avoid open-ended or easily-deferrable schedules so replacements proceed quickly and equitably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of water system control over full service lines
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should presume water systems have control over full service lines (owner-side and utility-side) as in the 1991 LCR, rather than narrowly defining ‘control’ to permit avoidance of replacements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt the 1991 definition of control or equivalent presumption; require primacy states to adopt rules stating systems are presumed to have control; institute conditions for primacy or alternate measures if local authority obstructs replacement; create processes to challenge and verify claims of lack of access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: Lead connector, lead service line, and connectors treated as service lines when >2 feet
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify definitions of lead connector and LSL, include lead connectors of any length in inventories, and treat 'connectors' exceeding two feet as service lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define connectors explicitly (including short lead connectors), require inventorying of all lead connectors, require verification of non‑lead service lines, and consider galvanized lines and lead materials in definitions; respond to EPA's specific requests about connector length and definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require replacement of lead connectors and galvanized replacements (GRRs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Service lines and connectors subject to mandatory replacement should include lead connectors and galvanized replacements that can act as lead sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include connectors of any length in the mandatory replacement scope; replace galvanized-to-lead-replacement (GRR) segments that may contain trapped lead; clarify replacement obligations and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit partial lead service line replacement as acceptable long-term solution
rubrics_metrics.description: Partial LSL replacements should not be allowed to substitute for full replacements and should not be used to avoid replacing customer‑side portions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require full-line replacement; if partial replacements occur due to emergency or technical constraints, impose strict conditions and timelines to complete full replacement, and require notification and interim protective actions (e.g., filters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit charging customers for full LSL replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: The LCRI must prohibit water systems from charging customers for full service line replacements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibit cost-sharing that would shift replacement costs to homeowners or tenants; justify through SDWA, Fair Housing Act, and Title VI authorities and environmental justice concerns; disallow programs that rely on homeowner payments as an access barrier.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA guidance and preference for replacement materials—prefer copper over plastics
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should guide selection of replacement materials, urging use of copper rather than plastics, and take steps to ensure chosen materials are safe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend copper because of lifecycle, durability, and to avoid contamination from plastics (hazardous chemicals, micro/nanoplastics); avoid PVC and CPVC where possible; consider long-term costs and the reduced need for future replacements with copper; require standards that account for contaminants that could leach from replacement materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid specific problematic plastics (PVC, CPVC) for service lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Among plastic materials, EPA should explicitly discourage or avoid use of PVC and CPVC for replacement service lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight concerns about degradation, toxic releases (including during fires), microplastics, and lifecycle harms; encourage research and restrictions on these materials in replacement programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA-funded studies to support material selection decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should undertake or fund studies necessary for state and local governments to make sound decisions about replacement service line materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies should evaluate leaching, lifecycle impacts, long-term durability, health consequences, and appropriate action levels for contaminants introduced by replacement materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead pipe disposal requirements and concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Address safe and environmentally sound disposal of removed lead pipes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish disposal standards and guidance to prevent environmental contamination during handling, transport, recycling or disposal of lead pipe material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service Line Replacement Plans (§141.84(c)) must be strengthened
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen and specify required contents of Service Line Replacement Plans so plans are actionable and protective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require detailed schedules, mandatory minimum annual replacements, funding plans, community engagement strategies, verification protocols, and enforcement mechanisms; respond to EPA’s specific requests for comment on plan requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance dates: accelerate implementation (≤1 year preferable)
rubrics_metrics.description: The LCRI’s compliance date should be less than three years after promulgation—ideally one year—so protections take effect sooner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make administrative provisions effective immediately or nearly so; align compliance dates with available federal funding to accelerate LSLR and other protections; argue practicability of earlier effective dates for most provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower lead action level (LAL) to ≤5 ppb and raise percentile benchmark above 90th
rubrics_metrics.description: A lead action level lower than 10 ppb is necessary; recommend reducing to no more than 5 ppb and using a percentile higher than the 90th for compliance assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower LAL to better prevent adverse health effects; use a higher percentile benchmark (e.g., >90th) because the 90th allows up to 10% of sites to remain highly exposed; demonstrate feasibility and public-health rationale; adjust monitoring and trigger actions accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require immediate distribution of certified filters to all consumers after any LAL exceedance
rubrics_metrics.description: Filters certified to reduce lead and replacement cartridges, with instructions, should be delivered to all consumers at no charge within 30 days of any LAL exceedance (the comments argue within 30 days; EPA proposed 60).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver NSF/ANSI‑certified filters and supplies to all customers, prioritize consumers served by LSLs/GRRs/unknowns, and continue replacement cartridges until two consecutive monitoring periods show no exceedance; do not allow states to substitute other actions for filters in the interim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require filter plans and expedited delivery and distribution mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Water systems should create and submit filter plans to states after exceedance, and must facilitate filter distribution to all consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans must specify logistics for rapid delivery, replacement cartridge schedules, instructions, language access, and verification of receipt/use; ensure access for low-English-proficiency and low-literacy consumers via translations and community partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher protections and actions after a single LAL exceedance (not multiple)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional actions should be required after one LAL exceedance rather than waiting for multiple exceedances (EPA proposed three in five years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trigger immediate protections (filters, outreach, CCT review, accelerated LSLR) after one exceedance; require states to augment actions but not to replace the mandatory federal response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentile benchmark feasibility: adopt percentile higher than 90th
rubrics_metrics.description: A percentile higher than the 90th percentile would better prevent adverse health effects and is technically feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess compliance using a higher percentile and demonstrate sampling/analytic capacity to support this metric; adapt monitoring protocols to maintain statistical validity at higher percentiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service line and connector inventories: initial inventory, annual updates, and public availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Require comprehensive initial inventories, annual updates, public posting, and validation of inventories, including deadlines and material identification requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventories must include leads, connectors, GRRs, and unknowns; require verification activities, validation deadlines, public access to inventory data, and procedures for correcting inventory errors; implement penalties or oversight for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation deadlines, material identification, and verification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Set explicit deadlines for validating inventories and identifying materials of unknown service lines, and require states/systems to meet these deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines should be short and enforceable; require verification by excavation, records review, or other reliable methods; require reporting of methods and uncertainty; require prompt follow-up for unknowns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacements in systems reporting only non-LSLs should be addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems that report only non-LSLs must still be required to validate and verify those claims and perform replacements where lead is found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept unverifiable claims of no LSLs; require physical verification and corrective actions if lead is found despite prior reporting of non-LSL status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small system flexibility should not weaken protections; strengthen POU device requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: While recognizing small systems' constraints, flexibility must not undermine public health protections; require stronger point-of-use (POU) device requirements and annual monitoring, eliminating long waivers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate nine-year monitoring waiver; require annual monitoring for small systems; require certification, maintenance, and reporting for POU devices; treat extensions as creating 'unreasonable risk to health' unless strictly justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tap sampling: revised tier definitions and tightened sampling protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise tier definitions, require improved sampling protocols (e.g., wide-mouth bottles), and tighten procedures to improve representativeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require both first- and fifth‑liter sampling at Tier 3 sites (particularly those served by LSLs), set maximum stagnation times, adopt wide-mouth collection bottles where appropriate, allow customer-requested supplemental monitoring, and require public data release of sampling results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require both first- and fifth-liter sampling at Tier 3 sites
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should require both first- and fifth-liter sampling at Tier 3 sites to better characterize water from service lines and detect lead from stagnation within lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify sampling protocols (bottle types, stagnation times); require Tier 3 sites (LSL-served) to have both liter samples analyzed to capture service-line contributions to lead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit triennial and nine-year reduced tap monitoring periods
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must prohibit triennial and nine-year reduced tap monitoring periods because these undermine timely detection of exceedances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require more frequent sampling cycles for systems at risk or with LSLs; remove long monitoring waivers that delay detection and response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make sampling data publicly available and increase transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Require sampling data to be made publicly accessible and timely, and create a national web-based portal for public access to drinking water sampling data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require direct electronic reporting of raw monitoring data to EPA, public dashboards, and system-level dissemination to communities, especially outreach to affected households and EJ communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify communication and public education messaging about sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: Address confusing messaging regarding sampling and public education; materials should clearly explain sampling results, risks, and next steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require clear content standards for public education, translated templates, plain-language materials, and multiple outreach modes (phone, text, email, door hangers, community partners) to ensure effective reach, especially for low-English-proficiency or low-literacy populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public education and outreach must include clear, accurate, robust information on tap-level risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Public education/public notification materials must include clear, accurate, and robust information regarding risks of lead exposure at individual taps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials must explain health risks, protective actions (e.g., POU filters), be translated, prioritize EJ communities, require annual outreach independent of 90th percentile performance, and specify content and speed/manner of notifications after sampling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of individual tap monitoring results: speed, manner, and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must notify individuals of tap-level monitoring results quickly, via appropriate channels, and include required content explaining risk and remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set timelines for notification, require multiple contact methods, provide plain-language explanations and instructions (including filter use), and ensure translated notices for limited-English-proficiency consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer Confidence Report (CCR) content must be revised and strengthened
rubrics_metrics.description: CCR requirements are insufficient and misleading; the rule should change CCR content to provide clearer, non-misleading information, including school sampling and service line materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require CCR statements to include school sampling requirements, service line material disclosures, action level exceedance information, and clear guidance on what consumers should do; make CCR information accessible and understandable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schools and child care facilities: adopt 'Filter First' or rigorous testing/remediation
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Filter First' approach (install and maintain certified filtration) is the best way to protect children; otherwise require robust, frequent testing and remediation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require either (a) installation and ongoing maintenance of POU filtration stations and annual testing of those stations, or (b) twice‑per‑year sampling of every outlet used for drinking/cooking and remediation for outlets above 1 ppb; limit waivers to legally required and properly maintained filtration programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: School/childcare sampling results must be publicly available and disseminated to parents and staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Require public availability and effective dissemination of school and childcare sampling results to enable community awareness and action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish results in accessible formats, directly notify parents/guardians/employees, include outlet-level data, and ensure identification of facility and related test results for accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate five-year deferral of corrosion control treatment (CCT) actions or narrow it
rubrics_metrics.description: The five-year deferral of CCT actions (§141.81(f)) fails to protect public health and must be eliminated or substantially narrowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If retained, narrow deferral to only certain limited study types; require criteria for eligibility, prevent avoidance of 100% LSL/GRR replacement, and remove blanket time delays that postpone feasible protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify and strengthen OCCT (optimized corrosion control treatment) definitions and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify the LCRI's definition of OCCT and modify inconsistent provisions so that OCCT determination and implementation are robust and protective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistent OCCT definition across §§ 141.2, 141.81; require standardized methods for determining OCCT, transparent reporting, and mandatory implementation where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen conduct and transparency of CCT studies
rubrics_metrics.description: CCT studies should be strengthened: require testing of more orthophosphate concentrations, measure additional water quality parameters, and ensure transparency and standardized protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require CCT studies to test a range of orthophosphate concentrations, measure parameters necessary to determine OCCT, make study data publicly available, prohibit use of noncompliant CCT studies for determining OCCT, and eliminate metal coupon studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate metal coupon studies and require more representative corrosion testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Metal coupon studies should be eliminated because they are not sufficiently representative of distribution/system conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require alternatives that reflect real system scales and conditions; require transparency, reproducibility, and use of studies that inform safe orthophosphate use and other CCT choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for lead dioxide (PbO2) scales and distribution-system impediments to orthophosphate CCT
rubrics_metrics.description: The LCRI should account for PbO2 scales as both a possible CCT and a possible impediment to safe orthophosphate use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require identification of PbO2 scale presence, appropriate testing, and consideration in OCCT decisions; require additional monitoring where PbO2 is suspected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require re-optimization of CCT after action level exceedances and ongoing duty to re-optimize
rubrics_metrics.description: All systems with CCT should have an ongoing duty to re-optimize CCT after action level exceedances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandate re-optimization procedures, timelines, and reporting after exceedances; do not allow medium/small systems to be excused from consequences of exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand water quality parameter monitoring (WQP) and simplify/transparent requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: WQP monitoring should be expanded, simplified, and made more transparent to support OCCT and detect changes that affect lead release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require additional parameters, standardized sampling/analytical methods, public reporting of WQP data, and link WQP results to CCT and LSLR decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution system and site assessment (find-and-fix) must be robust
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen requirements for distribution system and site assessment (formerly find-and-fix) to identify and mitigate lead sources promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require systematic assessments, timely corrective actions, documentation, and public reporting of distribution-system problems and remediation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower the lead practical quantitation limit (PQL)
rubrics_metrics.description: The lead PQL should be lowered to reflect current scientific and laboratory methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt lower PQLs consistent with modern analytical capability to improve detection of low-level lead and support stricter action levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create incentives and address shortages of CCT experts
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should create incentives to address identified shortages of CCT experts so systems can implement OCCT and CCT studies effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use funding, training programs, technical assistance, and certification pathways to expand qualified CCT expertise, especially for small and medium systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA should establish a Maximum Contaminant Level (MCL) for lead
rubrics_metrics.description: The SDWA requires EPA to set an MCL if it is feasible to ascertain the level of lead; the agency should establish an MCL for lead rather than rely solely on treatment techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present legal and technical rationale that an MCL is feasible, ensure MCL setting protects public health, and align monitoring and enforcement to support an MCL approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic and funding guidance: LSLR costs are feasible and should not make bills unaffordable
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's economic analysis shows reasonable per-LSLR costs; water systems can replace all LSLs without making bills unaffordable using available funding and rate strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximize federal funding (especially for disadvantaged communities), use non-ratepayer funding sources, adopt equitable rate structures, and leverage cost-reduction strategies available to water systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require direct electronic reporting of raw monitoring data and enhanced enforcement/transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must implement and require direct electronic reporting of violations and raw monitoring data so EPA can increase compliance oversight and communities receive timely, accurate information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandate electronic submission of full monitoring datasets, create national web-based portal for public access, require prompt reporting of service line disturbance notifications, and include incentives and enforcement mechanisms to improve compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create incentives to promote compliance outside enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: The final LCRI must include incentives (in addition to enforcement) for water systems to comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incentives may include funding priorities, technical assistance, public recognition, or other mechanisms that promote timely replacement and treatment adoption; pair incentives with reporting and transparency to encourage adherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen Environmental Justice (EJ) protections
rubrics_metrics.description: The LCRI must be strengthened to prevent disproportionate harm to communities of color and low-wealth communities; address renter harms and ensure equitable implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require systems to pay for full LSL replacements (no homeowner cost-sharing), prioritize outreach and replacements in EJ communities, require translations and culturally appropriate outreach, ensure landlords cannot shift costs to tenants, and require EJ analyses and mitigation measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require translation support and outreach for limited-English-proficiency and low-literacy populations
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should provide translated templates and require translation assistance so public education materials reach limited-English-proficiency and low-literacy individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide templates, encourage partnerships with community-based organizations and places of worship, require primacy states to provide translation support as a condition of primacy, and require multi-modal outreach to reach diverse populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and recordkeeping: expand inventory reporting and state record requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand inventory reporting to include lead connectors and non-lead service lines and require states to maintain documentation of determinations and implementation decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require states to keep records related to distribution system/site assessments, determinations of more stringent implementation, approvals related to reduced compliance monitoring, and provide EPA access; reduce reporting complexity and require raw data submission to EPA to improve oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: School/childcare waivers limited to well-maintained filter programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Waivers from sampling requirements for schools/childcare should be limited to locations where certified POU filters are required by law and properly maintained/tested at least annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not broadly waive sampling; require annual testing to ensure filters function and maintain documentation to support any waiver; limit waivers to legally mandated and verified filtration programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow states discretion only to add actions, not substitute for mandatory federal actions after exceedances
rubrics_metrics.description: States may determine additional appropriate actions tailored to systems but should not be allowed to substitute their actions for mandatory federal requirements such as filter provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State-determined actions must be in addition to federal required actions; EPA should not allow states to authorize actions that leave consumers exposed longer than federally required interventions.
